report_name: 'n0n' Extortion Group Claims Breach of Visa, Mastercard, JPMorgan

threat_actors.name: n0n
threat_actors.description: A data extortion group that claims to have breached and stolen sensitive data from Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase. The group's modus operandi is to exfiltrate data and threaten to leak it, without deploying ransomware for file encryption. The claims regarding this incident are unverified.
threat_actors.goals: To extort money from victim organizations by threatening to leak stolen data.

attack_patterns.name: Automated Exfiltration
attack_patterns.description: The n0n group's primary tactic is data exfiltration for the purpose of extortion, as stated in the report.

identities.name: Visa
identities.description: A major financial institution and payment card company allegedly breached by the 'n0n' group. The claim is unverified.

identities.name: Mastercard
identities.description: A major financial institution and payment card company allegedly breached by the 'n0n' group. The claim is unverified.

identities.name: JPMorgan Chase
identities.description: A major financial institution allegedly breached by the 'n0n' group. The claim is unverified.

indicators.name: Anomalous Data Exfiltration Volume
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous High Volume Outbound Traffic
id: 7e8c1f4a-9b0d-4c6e-8a1b-3d5f7a9b0c2d
status: experimental
description: Detects an unusual volume of data being sent to a single external destination, which could indicate data exfiltration.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-16
references:
  - https://pasqualepillitteri.it/en/news/34013/n0n-group-claims-attack-on-visa-mastercard-and-jpmorgan
tags:
  - attack.t1020
  - attack.exfiltration
logsource:
  category: firewall
level: medium
detection:
  selection:
    sc_bytes|gt: 100000000 # 100 MB
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects anomalous data flows to unknown external hosts, which could be indicative of data exfiltration as practiced by groups like n0n. This is based on the report's mention of monitoring for such patterns with DLP systems.

indicators.name: Anomalous Database API Access
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Large Data Response from API
id: 1b2c3d4e-5f6a-4b9c-8d7e-9f0a1b2c3d4e
status: experimental
description: Detects unusually large data responses from internal database or customer data APIs, which could indicate unauthorized data retrieval.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-16
references:
  - https://pasqualepillitteri.it/en/news/34013/n0n-group-claims-attack-on-visa-mastercard-and-jpmorgan
tags:
  - attack.t1020
  - attack.collection
logsource:
  category: webserver
level: medium
detection:
  selection:
    sc_bytes|gt: 50000000 # 50 MB
    cs_uri_stem|contains:
      - '/api/v1/customer_profiles'
      - '/api/data_export'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects anomalous access to large databases via API queries, as suggested by the report's mention of UEBA and monitoring database query APIs.
